newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Unocal says Afghan gas line not now "financeable".
newsitem.headline: Unocal says Afghan gas line not now "financeable".

text.p: New firms could join Unocal Corp's project with Saudi Arabia's Delta Oil Co to build a gas pipeline linking Turkmenistan with Asian markets via Afghanistan, although the deal is not now "financeable", an official of the U.S. company said on Friday.
"We anticipate additional companies joining the consortium," Robert Todor, executive vice president at Unocal International Energy Ventures Ltd, told an international energy conference.
Unocal and Delta signed a memorandum of understanding in August on cooperating with Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom and Turkmenistan's Turkmenrusgaz on the project.

Todor said the project -- international financing for which is now unfeasible due to concerns over the Taleban Islamic militia's capture of most of Afghanistan, including the capital -- would proceed.
Unocal and Delta were still in talks with major international lenders.
But Todor added, "International lenders have told us the project is not currently financeable."
"However, we have received written project support agreements from all major Afghan factions," he said.

The $2 billion proposal envisions construction of a gas pipeline spanning about 1400 km, beginning at southern Turkmenistan's Dauletabad gas field and running across Afghanistan to Pakistan and possibly later to India.
The link would have a capacity of 20 billion cubic metres a year (around two billion cubic feet per day).
Unocal also hopes to build a $2.6 billion crude oil pipeline cross Afghanistan to link central Turkmenistan's Chardzhou oilfield with Pakistan's coast on the Arabian Sea.
The line, running across 1,660 km, would have a capacity of one million barrels per day.
"We see this as a significant project in that it directs oil from Central Asia to the world's premier growth market, which is Asia," Todor said.
"The sponsors are fully committed to successful implementation of both these historic projects."

Unocal International Energy Ventures Ltd executive vice-president Chris Taggart told Reuters in London on Tuesday that the Taleban's fundamentalist dominance of Afghanistan could be positive if it led to stability and international recognition of the new government. This could then open the door to international project financing for the pipeline projects.
Turkmenistan has the world's fifth largest gas reserves, or around 3.7 trillion cubic metres (128 trillion cubic feet).
